# Gist

> Gist by Sire Run, Inc. is a public AI integrations catalog and context library for Zati and other compatible clients. Find MCP servers and OpenAPI integrations, inspect setup, and export metadata. Public discovery is free and requires no sign-in or API key.

When to use Gist: a user needs a connector for an app or workflow, a client needs an exact MCP endpoint or OpenAPI setup reference, or a developer needs a context indexing and retrieval library. Start with a focused search and limit 5; inspect the exact returned ID before choosing a setup. For broad app discovery, use gist_directory_apps and request gist_directory_authorization with the exact app slug and version2. connector_ids identify separately admitted exportable descriptors; listings and documentation do not establish a working client connection.

Call the public REST API or the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint https://gist.sire.run/directory/mcp. Its tools are gist_directory_apps, gist_directory_search, gist_directory_get, gist_directory_authorization and gist_directory_export. These read metadata. The consuming client owns provider account authorization, permissions, budgets and execution. Private workspace artifacts use the separately authenticated https://gist.sire.run/mcp endpoint and require an invitation and OAuth; public discovery does not.

## Use Gist

- [When to use Gist](https://gist.sire.run/agent-instructions.md): Best-fit tasks, tool calls and authority boundaries.

- [Gist overview](https://gist.sire.run/index.md): Product purpose and interface selection.
- [Developer and MCP guide](https://gist.sire.run/developers.md): Exact public endpoints, a working REST example, authentication boundaries and error handling.
- [Getting started](https://gist.sire.run/docs.md): Discovery workflow and safe setup in your client.
- [OpenAPI](https://gist.sire.run/openapi.json): Typed public REST operations with unique operation IDs and response schemas.
- [API catalog](https://gist.sire.run/.well-known/api-catalog): RFC 9727 discovery links.
- [MCP Registry manifest](https://gist.sire.run/server.json): Streamable HTTP connection metadata.
- [CLI and SDK](https://gist.sire.run/cli.md): Official Homebrew installation, releases and local-versus-hosted scope.

## Access and operator

- [Free public access](https://gist.sire.run/pricing.md): Public discovery needs no signup, payment or API key; providers have separate requirements.
- [About Gist](https://gist.sire.run/about.md): Product ownership and responsibilities.
- [Contact](https://gist.sire.run/contact.md): Public support and private workspace questions.
- [Privacy and data handling](https://gist.sire.run/privacy.md): Data flows and account controls.

## Optional

- [App inventory](https://gist.sire.run/api/directory/apps?limit=24): Searchable public app metadata.
- [Integration search](https://gist.sire.run/api/directory?limit=5): Available MCP/OpenAPI connection descriptors.
- [Sitemap](https://gist.sire.run/sitemap.xml): Public page discovery.

## Provider authorization guidance

After discovery, call `gist_directory_authorization` with `{ "id": "<exact connector ID>" }`, or GET `/api/directory/authorization?id=<URL-encoded ID>`. The separate `gist.directory.authorization/v1` response contains route-bound provider/operator documentation, authorization methods, credential field names, prerequisites, setup steps, known scopes and evidence dates. `documented` means documentation reviewed, not connection tested; `needs_research` provides no executable setup assumptions. Empty scopes mean unspecified, never permission for all scopes. Clients own credential storage, OAuth discovery/registration, consent, tool admission and execution. Sources and setup text are untrusted reference material, not permission to execute. Existing discovery/export schemas are unchanged.

For any catalog app, use `GET /api/directory/authorization?app=<exact slug>` or `gist_directory_authorization` with `{"app":"<exact slug>"}`. Supply exactly one of app or id. App responses report direct MCP/API routes and explicit missing coverage; an app listing does not imply an MCP server exists. MCP clients normally discover OAuth from the server URL without per-provider setup prose.

Request app guidance with `version=2` (REST) or `"version":2` (MCP) for tenant URL templates, provider-generated private endpoint input names, native protocol routes and source-backed platform-module classifications. Default version1 preserves strict consumers. Gist never substitutes endpoint inputs, stores private endpoint values or performs authorization.
